sentences.n: أَبْشِرُوا literally means 'receive glad tidings, rejoice' (form IV of بَشِرَ); the captain uses it with bitter irony to announce the crew's own destruction — a register of dark humor rather than a scribal slip.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ أَيُّهَا الرَّئِسُ أَخْبِرْنَا بِمَا رَأَى النَّاظُورُ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu ayyuhā al-raʾisu akhbirnā bi-mā raʾā al-nāẓūru
sentences.l: So I said, 'O captain, tell us what the lookout saw.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي اِعْلَمْ أَنَّنَا تِهْنَا فِي يَوْمٍ هَاجَتْ عَلَيْنَا الْأَرْيَاحُ وَلَا هَدَي الرِّيحُ إِلَّا بُكْرَةَ النَّهَارِ وَأَقَمْنَا يَوْمَيْنِ وَتِهْنَا فِي الْبَحْرِ وَلَنَا تَائِهِينَ إِحْدَى عَشَرَ يَوْمًا مِنْ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةِ وَلَا لَنَا رِيحٌ يُرْجِعُنَا إِلَى مَا نَحْنُ قَاصِدِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā sayyidī iʿlam annanā tihnā fī yawmin hājat ʿalaynā al-aryāḥu wa-lā hadā al-rīḥu illā bukrata al-nahāri wa-aqamnā yawmayni wa-tihnā fī al-baḥri wa-lanā tāʾihīna iḥdā ʿashara yawman min tilka al-laylati wa-lā lanā rīḥun yurjiʿunā ilā mā naḥnu qāṣidīna
sentences.l: He said, 'O my lord, know that we lost our way on a day when the winds rose against us, and the wind did not calm until the early morning; and we stayed two days, and we wandered lost at sea — eleven days now, from that night — with no wind to bring us back to where we were heading.'
sentences.i: He answered, 'Know, my lord, that we went astray on a day when a great gale rose against us and did not die down till the following daybreak. Then we lay becalmed for two days, drifting lost upon the sea — eleven days now, since that night — with no wind to carry us back onto our course.'
sentences.n: هدي: the consonants ه-د-ي properly spell 'to guide,' which makes no sense here ('the wind did not guide...'). This is most likely a phonetic, defective spelling of هَدَأَ, 'to calm down, abate,' with the medial hamza weakened to a glide and simply written يـ — a recognised Middle Arabic feature. We vocalise and translate on that reading, though it remains a considered guess rather than a certainty. — قاصدين: as predicate of the pronoun نحن, Classical grammar would want the nominative plural قَاصِدُونَ; this text, like everyday spoken Arabic, instead levels the sound masculine plural to the oblique-looking ending ـِين regardless of syntactic case. This is the first clear instance of a pattern that recurs below (see هالكين); we will not re-explain it every time.

sentences.t: وَأخِرَ النَّهَارِ غَدًا نَصِلُ إِلَى جَبَلِ حَجَرٍ أَسْوَدَ وَهُوَ يُسَمَّى حَجَرَ الْمِغْنَاطِيسِ
sentences.tr: wa-ākhira al-nahāri ghadan naṣilu ilā jabali ḥajarin aswada wa-huwa yusammā ḥajara al-mighnāṭīsi
sentences.l: 'And at the end of the day — tomorrow — we shall reach a mountain of black stone, which is called the Magnetic Stone.'
sentences.i: 'And by the close of tomorrow we will reach a mountain of black rock, called the Magnetic Mountain.'

sentences.t: وَتَجُرُّنَا الْمِيَاهُ غَصْبًا إِلَى تَحْتَهُ فَتَنْشَقُّ الْمَرْكَبُ وَيَرُوحُ كُلُّ مِسْمَارٍ فِي الْمَرْكَبِ إِلَى الْجَبَلِ وَ يَلْتَصِقُ إِلَيْهِ لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى رَكَّبَ فِي حَجَرِ الْمِغْنَاطِيسِ سِرًّا وَهُوَ أَنَّ جَمِيعَ الْحَدِيدِ يَذْهَبُ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-tajurrunā al-miyāhu ghaṣban ilā taḥtahu fa-tanshaqqu al-markabu wa-yarūḥu kullu mismārin fī al-markabi ilā al-jabali wa-yaltaṣiqu ilayhi li-anna allāha taʿālā rakkaba fī ḥajari al-mighnāṭīsi sirran wa-huwa anna jamīʿa al-ḥadīdi yadhhabu ilayhi
sentences.l: 'And the waters draw us against our will down beneath it, and the ship splits apart, and every nail in the ship goes off to the mountain and clings to it, because God Most High has built into the Magnetic Stone a secret — which is that all iron goes toward it.'
sentences.i: 'The current will drag us helplessly down to its foot; the ship will split apart, and every nail in her will tear loose and fly to the mountain, clinging fast to it — for God, Most High, has set a hidden power into the Magnetic Stone, by which all iron is drawn to it.'
sentences.n: ركب here is form II رَكَّبَ, 'to install, build into, compose,' not form I 'to ride' — God has 'built in' a secret power. سرا stands as an accusative of specification ('a secret [power]'), which the following أن-clause then glosses.

sentences.t: وَفِي ذَلِكَ الْجَبَلِ حَدِيدٌ كَثِيرٌ لَا يَعْلَمُهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ تَعَالَى حَتَّى أَنَّهُ تَكَسَّرَ مِنْ قَدِيمِ الزَّمَانِ مَرَاكِبُ كَثِيرَةٌ عَلَى ذَلِكَ الْجَبَلِ
sentences.tr: wa-fī dhālika al-jabali ḥadīdun kathīrun lā yaʿlamuhu illā allāhu taʿālā ḥattā annahu takassara min qadīmi al-zamāni marākibu kathīratun ʿalā dhālika al-jabali
sentences.l: 'And on that mountain is iron in great abundance, known to none but God Most High — so much so that many ships have been wrecked, since ancient times, upon that mountain.'
sentences.i: 'That mountain holds iron beyond all counting, known only to God Most High; indeed so many ships have gone to wreck upon it since ancient times.'

sentences.t: وَمِمَّا يَلِي الْبَحْرَ قُبَّةٌ مِنْ النُّحَاسِ الْأَصْفَرِ مَعْقُودَةٌ عَلَى عَشَرَةِ أَعْمِدَةٍ وَفَوْقَ الْقُبَّةِ فَارِسٌ وَفَرَسٌ مِنَ النُّحَاسِ وَفِي يَدِ ذَلِكَ الْفَارِسِ رُمْحٌ مِنَ النُّحَاسِ مُعَلَّقٌ فِي صَدْرِهِ لَوْحٌ مِنْ رَصَاصٍ مَنْقُوشٌ عَلَيْهِ أَسْمَاءٌ وَطَلَاسِمُ
sentences.tr: wa-mimmā yalī al-baḥra qubbatun min al-nuḥāsi al-aṣfari maʿqūdatun ʿalā ʿasharati aʿmidatin wa-fawqa al-qubbati fārisun wa-farasun mina al-nuḥāsi wa-fī yadi dhālika al-fārisi rumḥun mina al-nuḥāsi muʿallaqun fī ṣadrihi lawḥun min raṣāṣin manqūshun ʿalayhi asmāʾun wa-ṭalāsimu
sentences.l: 'And what borders the sea is a dome of yellow copper, raised upon ten pillars, and above the dome a horseman and a horse of copper; and in that horseman's hand a lance of copper, hung on his chest a plaque of lead, engraved upon which are names and talismans.'
sentences.i: 'Where the mountain meets the sea stands a dome of yellow brass, raised on ten pillars, and atop the dome a horseman and horse cast in copper. In the horseman's hand is a copper lance, and hanging from his chest a leaden plaque engraved with names and talismans.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ مَا يُهْلِكُ النَّاسَ إِلَّا الرَّاكِبُ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْفَرَسِ وَمَا الْخَلَاصُ إِلَّا إِذَا وَقَعَ هَذَا الْفَارِسُ مِنْ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْفَرَسِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī ayyuhā al-maliku mā yuhliku al-nāsa illā al-rākibu ʿalā hādhihi al-farasi wa-mā al-khalāṣu illā idhā waqaʿa hādhā al-fārisu min ʿalā tilka al-farasi
sentences.l: 'And he said to me, "O king, nothing destroys the people except the rider upon this horse, and there is no deliverance except if this horseman falls from off that horse."'
sentences.i: 'He told me, "O king, it is the rider on this horse alone that brings the people to ruin, and the only deliverance is for this horseman to fall from his mount."'
sentences.n: الفرس is treated as grammatically feminine here (هذه الفرس), one of the recognised alternatives for this noun in Classical usage.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ يَا سَيِّدَتِي بَكَى الرَّئِسُ بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا فَتَحَقَّقْنَا أَنَّنَا هَالِكِينَ لَا مَحَالَةَ وَكُلُّ مِنَّا وَدَّعَ صَاحِبَهُ وَوَصَّى اِحْتِمَالًا أَنْ يَسْلَمَ فَلَمْ نَنَمْ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu yā sayyidatī bakā al-raʾisu bukāʾan shadīdan fa-taḥaqqaqnā annanā hālikīna lā maḥālata wa-kullu minnā waddaʿa ṣāḥibahu wa-waṣṣā iḥtimālan an yaslama fa-lam nanam tilka al-laylata
sentences.l: 'Then indeed, O my lady, the captain wept a violent weeping, and we became certain, beyond all doubt, that we were doomed; and each of us bade his companion farewell and left him instructions, in case he alone should be saved; and we did not sleep that night.'
sentences.i: 'Then, O my lady, the captain broke into bitter weeping, and we knew for certain, past all hope, that we were doomed. Each of us said his farewells to his companion and left his last wishes, in case that one alone should survive; and not one of us slept that night.'
sentences.n: هالكين again shows the same levelled plural ending noted earlier at قاصدين — Classical grammar would want the nominative هَالِكُونَ as predicate of أنّ.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا جَاءَ الصَّبَاحُ قَرُبْنَا إِلَى ذَلِكَ الْجَبَلِ وَسَاقَتْنَا الْمِيَاهُ غَصْبًا إِلَيْهِ فَلَمَّا صَارَتْ الْمَرَاكِبُ تَحْتَهُ اِنْفَكَّتْ وَطَلَعَتْ الْمَسَامِيرُ وَكُلُّ حَدِيدٍ فِيهَا طَلَبَ حَجَرَ الْمِغْنَاطِيسِ وَاشْتَبَكَ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā jāʾa al-ṣabāḥu qarubnā ilā dhālika al-jabali wa-sāqatnā al-miyāhu ghaṣban ilayhi fa-lammā ṣārat al-marākibu taḥtahu infakkat wa-ṭalaʿat al-masāmīru wa-kullu ḥadīdin fīhā ṭalaba ḥajara al-mighnāṭīsi wa-ashtabaka fīhi
sentences.l: Then when morning came, we drew near to that mountain, and the waters swept us against our will toward it; and when the ships came beneath it, they came apart, and the nails came loose, and every piece of iron in them sought the Magnetic Stone and clung fast to it.
sentences.i: When morning came, we drew near the mountain, and the current swept us helplessly toward it. As the ships passed beneath it they broke apart — the nails tore free, and every scrap of iron in them flew to the Magnetic Stone and stuck fast there.

sentences.t: وَعِنْدَ أخِرِ النَّهَارِ دُرْنَا حَوْلَهُ فَمِنَّا مَنْ غَرِقَ وَمِنَّا مَنْ نَجَا وَأَكْثَرُنَا غَرِقَ وَالَّذِينَ سَلِمُوا لَمْ يَعْلَمُوا بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا وَإِنَّمَا تَوَّهَتْهُم الْأَمْوَاجُ وَاخْتِلَافُ الرِّيَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿinda ākhiri al-nahāri durnā ḥawlahu fa-minnā man gharaqa wa-minnā man najā wa-aktharunā gharaqa wa-al-ladhīna salimū lam yaʿlamū baʿḍuhum baʿḍan wa-innamā tawwahathum al-amwāju wa-ikhtilāfu al-riyāḥi
sentences.l: And at the end of the day we circled around it; some of us drowned and some of us survived, though most of us drowned; and those who survived did not know one another, for it was only the waves and the shifting of the winds that had confused them.
sentences.i: By day's end we had been swept in circles around it. Some of us drowned and some survived, though most were drowned; and those who lived did not even recognize one another, so utterly had the waves and the shifting winds confounded them.
sentences.n: بعضهم بعضا is the standard idiom for 'one another.' توهتهم is form II of a root shared with تاه/وهى, 'to make lost, bewilder' — the point being that survivors from different ships never even sighted each other.

sentences.t: وَ أَمَّا أَنَا يَا سَيِّدَتِي فَنَجَّانِي اللَّهُ تَعَالَى لِمَا يُرِيدُ مِنْ شَقَاوَتِي وَعَذَابِي وَ بَلْوَتِي فَطَلَعْتُ عَلَى لَوْحٍ مِنَ الْأَلْوَاحِ فَضَرَبَتْهُ الرِّيحُ فَالْتَصَقَ إِلَى الْجَبَلِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā anā yā sayyidatī fa-najjānī allāhu taʿālā li-mā yurīdu min shaqāwatī wa-ʿadhābī wa-balwatī fa-ṭalaʿtu ʿalā lawḥin mina al-alwāḥi fa-ḍarabathu al-rīḥu fa-iltaṣaqa ilā al-jabali
sentences.l: But as for me, O my lady, God Most High saved me for what He still willed of my wretchedness, my torment, and my trial; so I climbed onto a plank, one of the planks, and the wind drove it, and it stuck fast against the mountain.
sentences.i: As for me, O my lady, God Most High spared me — only so that I might still meet the misery, torment, and trial He had willed for me. I clambered onto a plank, and the wind drove it against the mountain, where it lodged fast.
sentences.n: لما يريد من شقاوتي وعذابي وبلوتي is an ominous turn of phrase: being 'saved' here means being kept alive for further trials God still intends, not saved from them — a signal to the listener that harder tests still lie ahead.

sentences.t: فَأَصَبْتُ طَرِيقًا مُتَطَرِّقًا إِلَى أَعْلَاهُ كَهَيْئَةِ السَّلَالِمِ مَنْقُورَةً فِى الْجَبَلِ فَسَمَّيْتُ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-aṣabtu ṭarīqan mutaṭarriqan ilā aʿlāhu ka-hayʾati al-salālimi manqūratan fī al-jabali fa-sammaytu allāha taʿālā
sentences.l: So I found a path winding up to its top, in the manner of stairs, carved into the mountain; and I pronounced the name of God Most High.
sentences.i: There I found a path winding up toward its summit, like a flight of steps cut into the rock, and I spoke the name of God Most High.
sentences.n: طريق is treated here as grammatically feminine (hence منقورةً agreeing with it), a recognised Classical alternative for this noun. فسميت الله تعالى uses سمّى in its formulaic sense 'to pronounce, invoke [God's name]' — i.e. to say the Bismillah before a hazardous undertaking — rather than 'to name.'

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنْ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿan al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And dawn overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent from lawful speech.
sentences.n: The fixed narrative-frame formula that closes every night: unlike the surrounding first-person tale, it speaks of Shahrazad in the third person and addresses the reader directly, not 'my lady' within the story.
